props.title: The War Tapes
props.initialSlug: Soldiers film their own Iraq War experience

sections.content: The War Tapes revolutionized war documentaries by putting cameras directly in soldiers' hands during Operation Iraqi Freedom. Director Deborah Scranton gave three New Hampshire National Guardsmen digital cameras, creating unprecedented raw footage from inside the Iraq War. This DIY approach stands in stark contrast to embedded journalism seen in Control Room (2004) and builds on the soldier-perspective tradition of Dear America: Letters Home from Vietnam (1987). The result is brutally honest, showing everything from mundane base life to intense firefights, with soldiers processing their experiences in real-time.

sections.content: The impact of soldier-filmed combat footage transformed war documentation in the digital age. Generation Kill (2008) and Combat Obscura (2018) followed similar approaches, letting marines tell their own stories. These raw perspectives challenge the polished narratives of films like The Hurt Locker (2008), revealing the complex reality of modern warfare through unfiltered personal experiences.

What sets The War Tapes apart is its exploration of the psychological toll of combat. The three featured soldiers - Zack, Mike, and Steve - process trauma differently on camera, providing intimate insights into PTSD development. This groundbreaking approach influenced later works like Thank You for Your Service (2017) and Of Men and War (2014), establishing a new standard for depicting war's mental health impact. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Soldier-Created War Documentation

sections.content: The democratization of war documentation through personal cameras created a new genre of military footage. While The War Tapes pioneered this approach in Iraq, later films like Severe Clear (2009) and This Is War (2012) expanded on the format. Social media and smartphones have further transformed how we document conflict, as seen in contemporary Ukrainian soldiers sharing TikTok footage - a direct legacy of The War Tapes' innovative approach.
